what: Cinemark is one of the largest movie theatre chains in the United States and Latin America, with about 500 theatres and 5,700 screens. It earns money from tickets, food and drinks, and screen advertising.
customers: Moviegoers, film studios that rent its screens, and advertisers.
money: Ticket sales, shared with the film studios.
Popcorn, drinks and food, which carry much higher margins than tickets.
moat: Theatres in good locations and premium formats such as XD screens give it the best attendance per screen among large US chains. The strongest balance sheet in the industry let it get through the pandemic without the restructurings that hit rivals.
risks: Attendance has not recovered to pre-pandemic levels, and streaming keeps competing for viewers.
Results depend on the film slate; a year with few hits hurts badly.
Debt of $3.0B against $613M of equity is high.
Hollywood strikes or delays can empty the release calendar.
opportunities: Revenue reached $3.57B over the last twelve months, above every full year shown.
The 2026 and 2027 film slates are fuller than recent years.
Share count fell from 155M in 2024 to 134M in 2025.
Concessions spending per visitor keeps rising.
watch: Box office totals and attendance per screen.
view: Cinemark is the best operator in a structurally challenged industry. It came through the pandemic in better shape than any big rival, has the highest attendance per screen, and has started returning cash by buying back shares. Revenue over the last twelve months is above any recent year.

At about 16 times trailing earnings and 9 times EV/EBITDA, the market treats it as a mature business that may slowly shrink. I think that is roughly right: people still go to the cinema for big events, but the number of films that fill theatres is smaller than it was before streaming.

The investment turns on the film slate. A strong 2026–2027 calendar would lift earnings and cash flow, and the buybacks would compound that. I would call it fairly priced with an upside skew if Hollywood delivers; I would not pay up for it.
bull: A strong film slate lifts attendance and buybacks compound the gains.
bear: Streaming keeps attendance below pre-pandemic levels and debt weighs on returns.
